previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and GJ tube dependence was admitted after transfer for a malfunctioning feeding tube that was displaced and likely caused aspiration pneumonia. He was stabilized, and a new GJ tube was successfully placed via interventional radiology. Nutrition was resumed, resolving mild hypoglycemia, and all chronic medications, including antiretrovirals, were restarted through the tube. His respiratory status improved to baseline, and he was discharged to extended care with instructions to maintain tube care and medication routines.

EXAMINATION:  Chest radiograph

INDICATION:  History: ___ with sob, cough, chronic trach// eval for pna

TECHNIQUE:  Portable semi upright view of the chest

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___

FINDINGS: 

Lung volumes are low.  There is persistent diffuse multifocal bilateral
interstitial opacities, compatible with chronic lung disease.  However,
superimposed pneumonia is difficult to exclude in the appropriate clinical
setting.  A tracheostomy remains appropriately placed.  There is diffuse
gaseous distension of multiple bowel loops, unchanged.  No definite
pneumothorax or large pleural effusion.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is
obscured by adjacent opacities, but likely unchanged.  Interval removal
left-sided PICC.

Low lung volumes with persistent diffuse multifocal bilateral interstitial
opacities, likely chronic lung disease.  However, superimposed pneumonia is
difficult to exclude in the appropriate clinical setting

PROCEDURE:  1. Repositioning of right PICC.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: The patient was brought to the angiographic table and a
initial fluoroscopic spot image was obtained which demonstrated the PICC line
terminating in the internal jugular vein.  Then, a power flush technique was
utilized under fluoroscopic guidance and the PICC was repositioned to the low
SVC.
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. Existing right arm approach PICC with tip in the internal jugular
reposition to the low SVC with power flush

IMPRESSION: 

Successful PICC line repositioning.  The PICC is ready to use.
